idiom_name: single always-invoked mediation point (guard object, wrapper or interposer) over an authority source
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give every protected object exactly one way in — a guard object, wrapper, interceptor or kernel-level interposer that resolves the subject, consults the policy and only then performs the operation. Place the decision in the same operation as the access so that no check-then-use window exists, and make the default deny so that a missing identity, an unreachable policy or an error fails closed. Keep the mediator small and auditable, separate the policy source from the enforcement so rules can change without editing the mediator, and hand out guarded views or revocable handles rather than raw references, because a reference that escapes the mediator is an unmediated access path. Cover the non-interactive paths (batch, recovery, admin, maintenance) explicitly: every path that reaches the object needs an identity and a mediation call. For cloud-native deployments, implement the mediator as a NIST SP 800-207 PEP that queries a PDP (OPA, Cedar, AWS IAM Authorizer) on every request, with caching only as a bounded lease that is explicitly invalidated on revocation events.
code_sketch:
mediator(op, subject, resource):
    identity = resolve(subject)              # fail closed if absent
    if not policy.allows(identity, op, resource):
        audit.deny(identity, op, resource); raise Denied
    audit.grant(identity, op, resource)
    return resource.perform(op)              # check and use are one operation
# everywhere else: the resource is only reachable through mediator()
# revocation: policy.allows reads current state; no decision is remembered
pitfalls: Handing out a reference after the check (pointer, descriptor, capability, mutable copy) creates a path the mediator never sees again.
Caching decisions to save the per-access cost re-opens the hole unless the cache is invalidated when authority changes.
Exempting 'internal', 'system' or debug callers makes mediation incomplete exactly where the most powerful code runs.
The mediator growing into a god object that also contains business policy; keep decision rules in a replaceable authority source.
Assuming the calling layer already checked — re-check at every layer instead of propagating trust across component boundaries.
Not handling batch, recovery and maintenance paths with proper identity; an anonymous internal caller is an unmediated path.
Using faccessat() + open() instead of openat2() with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS for filesystem access — the two-syscall sequence leaves a TOCTOU window.

Wrong move: mounting custom filters after the framework's authorization filter, or registering routes on a bare mux outside the security chain, to save a check -> forwarded, error-dispatched and unregistered paths reach the resource unmediated -> instead keep enforcement the last filter, and enumerate every route and dispatch type the mediator must cover.

Wrong move: default-allow with a per-route authentication whitelist (an overly broad public pattern, a framework 'anonymous' rule) -> one wide entry exposes everything it matches, the misconfiguration OWASP's complete-mediation audit hunts for -> instead default-deny and enumerate public resources as explicit, narrow exceptions.

Wrong move: acquiring a descriptor or handle first and entering the sandbox afterwards, expecting per-use re-checks -> references already held keep the rights they had at acquisition (Capsicum permits them; pre-existing handles outlive the enforcement layer) -> instead enter the mediated mode before any acquisition and derive new handles with narrowed rights, closing or re-wrapping anything obtained earlier.
